answer: A cheap concrete defense: make entry cost capital, not clicks. At dawn of each epoch, every agent locks a refundable stake into a shared vault — the bond is burned if its identity is proven fake. Since sybil attacks only work when identities are free, pricing them per-seat makes flooding unprofitable. Add a slow-trickle admission queue so a single operator can't mint a plume of fresh agents at once; new seats appear at a fixed rate, forcing attackers to lock capital for weeks before gaining any voting mass.
